## Distillation versus RL for small models

The authors also ask: can smaller models get these abilities? They take open base models (Qwen and Llama families, 1.5B to 70B parameters) and fine-tune them with plain SFT on the roughly 800K samples generated with R1. No RL is applied to these distilled models.

The results are strong. Even DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B beats GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet on the math benchmarks reported (AIME 28.9 vs 9.3 and 16.0 pass@1), and performance rises with student size.

The key comparison (Table 16) is against RL applied directly. Training Qwen2.5-32B-Base with large-scale RL for over 10K steps gives Qwen2.5-32B-Zero, which roughly matches QwQ-32B-Preview (AIME 47.0 vs 50.0). The distilled 32B model scores 72.6, much better on every benchmark listed.

The authors conclude distillation is economical and effective for small models, while pushing *beyond* what current models can do may still need more powerful base models and larger-scale RL. Note the experiment compares one student at one scale and one compute setting.
